object_description: flat-roofed two-storey volume, largely glazed all round, aligned with the existing hall
geometry_property: two spatial layers along the long facades
open courtyard in the middle zone
design_condition: the volume is placed precisely in relation to the existing triple hall and adopts its orientation, its south facade continuing the north facade of the existing hall

positive: The volume is placed precisely in relation to the existing hall and adopts its orientation
Due to its moderate height and placement the building has little impact on the neighbourhood
The reorganisation of the access situation from the street is fundamentally positive
Separating pedestrian and driving traffic improves student safety and access to the existing hall
Relatively extensive outdoor areas with a high quality of stay are created
The main entrance with a large forecourt, central fountain and tree roofs invites lingering
The sports and lounge areas in the north are well greened and shaded
From the entrance area there is a view of the sports hall lowered by one floor
The cloakroom and shower facilities are largely functionally organised
The circulation areas are appropriately sized
The underground connection between the two halls is well solved
The three-sided lighting of the hall largely meets the requirement for optimal daylight
A pleasant atmosphere can be expected for the sports halls
The central zone is naturally lit by adding a courtyard with an outdoor climate
The upper floor structure is largely free of load-bearing or bracing walls
The floor plan typology has potential for a stimulating and flexible learning landscape
The volumetrics near rather small-scale residential buildings are well chosen
The redesign of the access situation and the northern open spaces is positive
The remaining surrounding areas are of high quality and skilfully designed
Ecologically valuable biodiverse green spaces are created with native trees and wild perennials
negative: The central parking lot could pose potential for conflict
The dual use of park fields as a gravel grass sports field is not practical
Gravel turf is hardly suitable for sport and has poor durability as a parking lane
The southern outdoor space appears hard and cleared out near the single-family houses
The different uses on the two floors cannot be seen in the facade design
The two separate equipment rooms do not correspond to the competition specifications
The underground connection collides with the existing external ramp
There is no information about the material used for the other sports rooms
An indoor-climate top-lit area could be more useful than the outdoor courtyard
The sparse explanations do not clarify how the art rooms are intended to work
How the partition wall between the halls fits the support system without affecting clearance is not shown
The dimensions of the rod elements are clearly too slim
Underfloor heating in the art rooms does not meet the client specifications
The proportion of glass significantly exceeds the permissible limit value
This raises questions regarding summer heat, glare protection and ecology
The profitability indicators are below the average of all projects examined
